problem: Real-time 3D scene graph generation methods rarely model semantic relations between objects (e.g. beside, on top of), and learned 3D scene graph methods depend on indoor-only 3D datasets, so they do not work outdoors or in real robot navigation.
motivation: Object relations could let LLM planners search more efficiently, but prior LLM-based scene-graph navigation (SayPlan, SayNav) was only run in indoor simulation with ground-truth semantics. Large 2D panoptic scene graph datasets cover both indoor and outdoor scenes, so lifting 2D predictions into 3D via SLAM avoids the need for 3D training data.
key_idea: Predict a 2D panoptic object-relation graph on each SLAM keyframe and fuse these graphs into a global layered 3D scene graph using LiDAR-inertial SLAM (LIO-SAM) pose graph and semantic voxel mapping.
insight: Fusing multi-view 2D predictions in 3D improves both object localization and relation correctness over single-frame predictions (object error down 11.6-37.1%; relation accuracy 56.67->83.33% indoor, 64.71->94.12% outdoor). Adding relations to the scene graph given to the LLM planner cut search time in all 6 paired real-robot trials (18-35%), e.g. the LLM visits only one table when chairs are 'beside' it. Evidence is small-scale (6 trials, 47 relations).
method: 3D semantic object extraction: LIO-SAM pose-graph SLAM gives keyframe poses; each keyframe point cloud gets labels from the 2D panoptic segmentation via pixel-to-point mapping, is voxelized, and voxel labels are fused by Bayesian update; Euclidean clustering of same-label voxels yields object nodes.
Loop-closure handling: when SLAM corrects poses, the affected semantic point clouds are relabeled into voxels and the object nodes are re-clustered.

2D panoptic scene graph generation: PSGFormer (one-stage) with a lighter Mask2Former ViT-Tiny backbone, trained on the PSG dataset, outputs masks, labels and relations over 133 object classes and 56 relations.

3D scene graph merging: each 2D graph is lifted to 3D via the point cloud, checked against existing 3D objects for label/mask consistency, and new nodes/edges are added or existing ones updated in the global graph.
Layered structure: manually defined hierarchy (site, regions such as rooms or outdoor areas separated by doors/roads, objects) that works indoors and outdoors.
SayNav integration: Graph2Nav replaces SayNav's ground-truth-based graph module; the scene graph with relations is turned into text prompts for GPT-3.5, and Nav2 executes the planned steps on a UGV.

setting.backbone: PSGFormer with Mask2Former ViT-Tiny (trained on PSG); GPT-3.5 (frozen) as SayNav planner
setting.training_data: PSG panoptic scene graph dataset (2D, 133 object classes, 56 relations); the LLM is used without training
setting.observation: RGB (RealSense D455) + Livox Mid-360 LiDAR with IMU
setting.action_space: LLM high-level plan steps (move to object, look around) executed by Nav2 path planning and low-level control
setting.privileged: none (sensor calibration is assumed; ground truth only used for evaluation)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark results. The paper reports custom real-world results: 3D object localization error (m) Graph2Nav vs single image: Indoor1 0.3867 vs 0.5898, Indoor2 0.2236 vs 0.2530, Outdoor1 0.3619 vs 0.5755, Outdoor2 0.8407 vs 1.0403; relation accuracy 83.33% indoor and 94.12% outdoor vs 56.67% and 64.71% for the 2D baseline; search time on 6 lab scenarios with vs without relations, from 165.0 to 124.8 s, 184.7 to 147.0 s, 222.6 to 163.8 s, 250.3 to 163.1 s, 152.6 to 111.4 s, and 166.4 to 136.3 s.
results: Fusing 2D panoptic scene graphs in 3D reduces object localization error by 11.62-37.12% and raises relation accuracy from 56.67% to 83.33% (indoor) and 64.71% to 94.12% (outdoor) against a single-image baseline. On a real UGV running SayNav with GPT-3.5, adding relations reduced search time by 18.09-34.84% in all 6 paired object-search trials in a lab.
limitations: Very small evaluation: 6 search trials in one lab, 47 hand-annotated relations, 67 measured objects, and no comparison against other navigation methods
The layered hierarchy is defined manually, and the relation and class vocabulary is fixed to the PSG dataset; small objects are hard to detect from far away
Relies on calibrated LiDAR-camera sensors and a remote GPT-3.5 call, with no success-rate metrics reported
